items.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence Use and Adolescent Mental Health
items.author: Jason M. Lavender
items.summary: This paper synthesizes recent literature on the relationships between GenAI use and adolescents’ mental health, with particular attention to problematic use and psychiatric vulnerabilities.
items.body:
ResearchPosted on rand.org Sep 28, 2026Published in: Current Pediatrics Reports, Volume 14, Article Number 16 (2026). DOI: 10.1007/s40124-026-00388-8

To synthesize recent literature on the relationships between generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) use and adolescents’ mental health, with particular attention to problematic use and psychiatric vulnerabilities.

Emerging evidence suggests associations between GenAI use and a range of adolescent mental health outcomes, including depression, anxiety, psychosis-related experiences, externalizing behaviors, eating disorder risk, and suicidality. Problematic patterns of use, including dependency and emotional reliance, may be particularly relevant among adolescents with preexisting psychiatric vulnerabilities. Current evidence suggests that these relationships may be bidirectional: psychological distress can motivate GenAI use for companionship, emotional support, or escape, while problematic use may reinforce maladaptive beliefs, displace real-world relationships, and amplify existing vulnerabilities. However, evidence remains predominantly cross-sectional, limiting causal inference.

GenAI may interact with and amplify underlying psychiatric vulnerabilities during adolescence, highlighting the importance of understanding patterns and motivations of use. Pediatricians and other clinicians caring for adolescents could consider not only the frequency of GenAI use but also motivations for use, problematic dependency, and socioemotional reliance. Identifying high-risk usage patterns of GenAI through longitudinal research, particularly among youth with preexisting psychiatric risks, may inform the development of tailored screening, intervention, and prevention strategies.

items.title: From Policy to Practice
items.author: Elizabeth D. Steiner
items.summary: We investigated the role that state policies related to preschool curriculum play in public school pre-K teachers’ reported curricula use across the United States.
items.body:
How State Policies Relate to Public Pre-K Teachers’ Curriculum Use

ResearchPosted on rand.org Sep 28, 2026Published in: National Institute for Early Education Research website (2026)

As many states expand the number of pre-K seats in public schools, policymakers are focused on better understanding the role of curriculum in ensuring high-quality early childhood education environments. By combining data from the National Institute for Early Education Research’s State of Preschool Yearbook with data from RAND's American Pre-K Teacher Survey, we investigated the role that state policies related to preschool curriculum play in public school pre-K teachers’ reported curricula use across the United States. We find substantial variation in the curricula teachers report using across states, and some differences across pre-K programs within states. In addition, specific state curriculum guidance appears to influence classroom curriculum use. When states required that teachers use specific curricula (rather than recommending curricula), teachers reported combining fewer curricula in their classrooms.

items.title: Private Equity Ownership and Artificial Intelligence Adoption by Hospitals in the United States
items.author: Yashaswini Singh
items.summary: We examined the association between private equity hospital ownership and the likelihood of artificial intelligence technology adoption.
items.body:
ResearchPosted on rand.org Sep 28, 2026Published in: Health Affairs Scholar, qxag261 (2026). DOI: 10.1093/haschl/qxag261

Private equity (PE) firms own a growing share of United States hospitals and claim that capital infusions support technology investment. We examined the association between PE hospital ownership and the likelihood of artificial intelligence (AI) technology adoption.

We linked the 2024 American Hospital Association Annual Survey to a database of PE acquisitions and exits. Mixed-effects logistic models estimated any, clinical, and operational AI adoption by hospital ownership type, adjusting for hospital and market characteristics. In secondary analyses, we examined challenges to AI implementation.

PE-owned hospitals had higher adjusted adoption of any AI (difference, 24.5 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, 11.2 to 37.8) and clinical AI (difference, 27.5 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, 14.0 to 41.1) than other for-profit hospitals but did not differ from not-for-profit hospitals. Operational adoption did not differ by ownership. In secondary analyses, not-for-profit hospitals reported any, cost and resource, and regulatory and safety challenges more often than PE-owned hospitals; PE-owned hospitals reported staff-training challenges more often than other for-profit hospitals.

PE-owned and not-for-profit hospitals had similar adoption of any and clinical AI, and both exceeded other for-profit hospitals, consistent with a capital access advantage that does not extend to the broader for-profit sector.

items.title: Researchers Are Not Blank Slates
items.author: Lori Uscher-Pines
items.summary: This paper examines the implementation of a researcher self-disclosure approach where researchers shared aspects of their identity and background in interviews with Latina and Black parents participating in a clinical trial on telelactation support.
items.body: Qualitative interviews are central to social research, yet the dynamics of rapport, power, and researcher reflexivity remain complex and underexplored. This paper examines the implementation of an intentional researcher self-disclosure approach where researchers shared aspects of their identity and background in interviews with Latina and Black parents participating in a clinical trial on telelactation support. Drawing on an equity-centered model, we adapted our interview guide to foster trust and richer dialogue. Comparative analysis of interviews conducted before and after this adaptation revealed increased depth and breadth of participant responses, particularly regarding cultural, community, and family influences on breastfeeding. Our findings highlight the potential and challenges of researcher self-disclosure, offering insights for more patient-centered and effective qualitative research. We share lessons learned and offer best practices for researchers who wish to incorporate this approach in their interviewing practice.

items.title: Healey pledges “new age of industrialisation” as Government backs British shipbuilding
items.summary: Two major maritime projects to be part of “new age of industrialisation” for Britain.
items.body:
Government backs British shipyards with multi-billion pound investment in three major maritime projects to strengthen national security, support skilled jobs and drive growth in every part of the UK.

Chancellor confirms three new floating docks for the Royal Navy’s submarine service at HM Naval Base Clyde will be built in Britain supporting Britain’s defence industrial base and securing key sovereign capabilities.

New marine research vessel to be built in a British shipyard, backing coastal communities, sustainable fishing and long-term economic growth.

British shipyards will be at the heart of two major maritime projects worth billions of pounds, helping to create high-skilled jobs, drive growth and strengthen the UK’s long-term industrial and national security capabilities.

Chancellor John Healey will pledge a “new age of industrialisation” for Britain today as he confirms the multi-billion pound projects will be built by British workers, supporting jobs and a pipeline of small British businesses.

Healey will confirm that the Royal Navy’s submarine service at HM Naval Base Clyde will receive three new floating docks - known as Programme Euston - through a UK-only competition, in light of their importance to national security and sovereign British industry.

The new facilities will provide crucial maintenance for the UK’s current and future fleet of nuclear submarines, allowing essential inspections, upgrades and repairs to be carried out.

In addition to this, the Chancellor has also committed to funding for a new marine research vessel to help protect our seas. Set to be operational in the early 2030s, it will continue the delivery of core research on our seas and oceans, replacing the current vessel which is nearing the end of its life.

The evidence it collects will help ensure the security of our seas, support sustainable fishing and give coastal communities confidence that fish stocks are being managed for the future.

Both projects will be delivered by UK companies, as part of a greater focus on how government spends taxpayers’ money to boost national security whilst also supporting British jobs and growth in local communities.

Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey said:

“Britain has a proud shipbuilding heritage, and every pound of this strategic investment in a critical sector is backing British jobs on the Clyde and businesses across the UK, supporting growth in every postcode.

“By backing British shipyards, we are not only boosting national security but also securing resilience in the industries that will drive growth today while building the capabilities the country needs for the future.”

Defence Secretary, Wes Streeting said:

“Defence spending should make Britain stronger in every sense. That means backing British by buying British wherever our industry can deliver.

“HM Naval Base Clyde is at the heart of our submarine service. Programme Euston will modernise it for decades to come, while backing British shipyards, workers and engineering.

“That is defence driving the reindustrialisation of Britain and strengthening our sovereign capability.”

items.title: UK Thwarts Suspected Terrorist Plot Against Base Used by US Bombers for Strikes on Iran
items.author: Chris Gordon
items.summary: An air base in England used by American bombers to strike Iran was the target of a suspected bomb plot, U.K. officials said Sept. 27. The post UK Thwarts Suspected Terrorist Plot Against Base Used by US Bombers for Strikes on Iran appeared first on Air & Space Forces Magazine .
items.body:
An air base in England where American bombers used to strike Iran are based was the target of a suspected bomb plot, U.K. officials said Sept. 27.

Five men were arrested on suspicion of terrorism and explosives offenses after being stopped close to RAF Fairford, police said, and explosive ordnance disposal technicians were dispatched to the scene. RAF Fairford is a British base currently hosting a dozen B-1B Lancer bombers, which have been stationed there for around seven months for strikes on Iran.

President Donald Trump said the suspects were “looking to do big damage” to the U.S. at RAF Fairford and called the arrests “fantastic” before boarding Air Force One on Sept. 27.

“We had them under view for a long time and we got them,” Trump added. “Working with Britain, it was an amazing job. We had them under investigation.”

The base has been under increased security for days, which included the placement of vehicles around the perimeter, people familiar with the matter said. The threat level at the base was raised before the suspects were arrested. A U.S. Air Force spokesperson declined to discuss specific force protection measures, citing operational security.

Explosive ordnance teams from the British Army were called in to inspect the scene, and helicopter video footage aired by multiple U.K. news outlets showed a robot and personnel inspecting three white vans near the base fence, with B-1Bs parked on base nearby.

“The safety and security of the public is our first priority, and I want people to know that we will always take every step necessary to protect our communities and keep our country safe,” British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said in a statement.

Police said they were called by a local after receiving a report about three suspicious vehicles near RAF Fairford, which is located in Gloucestershire in southwest England.

“At around 12:45 a.m. today … police received a call relating to three suspicious vehicles which appeared to be traveling towards the air base,” the Metropolitan Police, which investigates terrorism cases in the U.K., said in a Sept. 27 statement.

The U.K. government is still investigating the incident, counterterrorism officials said.

“We are in the early stages of an investigation, and five men remain in custody,” counterterrorism policing senior national coordinator Vicki Evans said. “As you would expect, we are working closely with our partners to understand the circumstances of the incident.”

RAF Fairford does not have permanent U.S. Air Force aircraft assigned there, but it has a wing dedicated to supporting U.S. operations and is considered the main U.S. bomber site in Europe, having regularly hosted U.S. aircraft for years.

“The 501st Combat Support Wing and our other U.K.-based wings remain vigilant and will take appropriate actions to ensure the safety and security of our U.S. service members, civilians, contractors, and their families,” the Air Force spokesperson said. “We constantly assess a variety of factors that determine what measures we institute or modify to protect our installations, our people, and their families.”

Roadblocks, large machinery, and armed police have been seen around the base. Eighty-five homes in the nearby village of Whelford were evacuated.

“The emergency services have well-rehearsed plans for dealing with major incidents,” Gloucestershire Police assistant chief constable Richard Ocone said. “A cordon is in place as a precaution and the public can expect to see an emergency services presence in the area for some time.”

The B-1Bs at Fairford were heavily used during Operation Epic Fury, the large-scale air campaign against Iran in the spring, when the base housed some two dozen bombers including B-52 Stratofortresses.

Since a shaky ceasefire in April, most of the B-1Bs have remained while the U.S. carried out occasional strikes, including at least one involving a B-1 from Fairford. The bombers have regularly conducted training sorties out of the U.K.

The U.K. government gave permission for the base to be used in strikes on Iran in March under former Prime Minister Kier Starmer, for what the U.K. considers collective self-defense strikes. Burnham reaffirmed that decision in July, and Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps warned the U.K. government that it considered Fairford a legitimate target for attack. The U.K. government said in July it was prepared to use the British armed forces to defend the base.

The U.S. Air Force said it would continue to cooperate with the U.K. government to ensure the safety of its bases in Britain. Another U.K. base with U.S. aircraft is RAF Lakenheath, which hosts F-35A Lightning II and F-15E Strike Eagle fighters that have deployed to the Middle East for operations against Iran. Lakenheath is also used as a stopover location for fighters heading to the Middle East from the U.S.

“The safety and security of our Airmen, families, and surrounding communities remains our highest priority,” the Air Force spokesperson said. “We remain in close coordination with our U.K. partners to help ensure the safety and security of both our military and local communities.”

items.title: Terror suspects wanted to do ‘big damage’ to air base used by US, Trump says
items.author: Toby Shepheard, Reuters
items.summary: British police on Sunday arrested five men on suspicion of explosive and terrorism offenses near an air base that hosts U.S. Air Force personnel.
items.body:
British police on Sunday arrested five men near an air base used by U.S. forces on suspicion of explosive and terrorism offenses after a tip that three vans were heading to the military airfield, which has been used to strike Iran.

U.S. President Donald Trump said the suspects had been looking to do “big damage” and had been under investigation by British and U.S. authorities.

British counter terrorism detectives leading the investigation said police received a call about three suspicious vehicles that appeared to be traveling towards RAF Fairford in the west of England in the early hours of Sunday.

Five men were arrested by armed officers and later held on suspicion of preparation of a terrorist act. Police said they believed the incident was now contained.

POLICE WORKING TO UNDERSTAND CIRCUMSTANCES

“We are in the early stages of an investigation, and five men remain in custody,” Counter Terrorism Policing Senior National Coordinator Vicki Evans said in a statement.

“As you would expect, we are working closely with our partners to understand the circumstances of the incident.”

Police said a 400-meter cordon was in place around the base as the bomb disposal unit investigated the vans. Local residents in 85 homes in a nearby village were evacuated, and armed officers were patrolling the site.

The British government, which has given authorization to the U.S. to use bombers based at Fairford to strike Iranian missile sites that were attacking ships in the Strait of Hormuz, said Prime Minister Andy Burnham was being updated on the incident.

“I know today’s incident near RAF Fairford will be deeply concerning for local residents and for many people following developments across the country,” Burnham wrote on X.

Britain said in July its armed forces were ready to protect the country from any attack after Iran’s Revolutionary Guards warned it not to allow U.S. bombers to fly from Fairford, saying any base used to launch attacks would be a legitimate target.

Police have not said who they believed was involved in Sunday’s alleged incident. An Iranian-linked motive is considered the most likely, a source familiar with the investigation said, while a Russian sabotage operation or an Islamist plot are also being looked at.

“The arrest in the UK was fantastic,” Trump told reporters, saying it was “an amazing job.”

“We had them under investigation. They were looking to do big damage to our port and working with the British worked out great. ... We had them under view for a long time, and we got them,” Trump added.

On Sunday morning the base was blocked by armed police while large machinery also prevented access. Reuters witnesses said security had been increased at other bases used by the U.S., with armored vehicles and soldiers at the gates of RAF Lakenheath and RAF Mildenhall in eastern England.

DECLARATION OF A MAJOR INCIDENT

“A cordon is in place as a precaution, and the public can expect to see an emergency services presence in the area for some time,” Gloucestershire Police Assistant Chief Constable Richard Ocone told reporters.

The Daily Mail website carried a photograph of five men without shirts who it said had been arrested.

A spokesperson for the U.S. Air Force declined to discuss specific force protection measures.

“The 501st Combat Support Wing and our fellow UK-based Wings remain vigilant and will take appropriate actions to ensure the safety and security of our U.S. service members, civilians, contractors, and their families,” the spokesperson said.

“We constantly assess a variety of factors that determine what measures we institute or modify to protect our installations, our people and their families.”

British ministers have also previously briefed providers of critical infrastructure on the threat posed by Russia, with the government increasingly concerned about possible sabotage operations and cyberattacks.

Russia denies mounting hybrid attacks on Western nations.

A British military air base in central England was broken into in June 2025 by the Palestine Action protest group, which has since been proscribed as a terrorist organization.

items.title: Ukraine’s deadly AI training platform for drone tech opens to UK companies
items.author: Katie Livingstone
items.summary: Ukraine opens wartime battlefield data to Britain through Avengers AI Labs, giving British companies access to data for AI drone development.
items.body:
KYIV, Ukraine — The British Ministry of Defence has struck a partnership with Ukraine’s Avengers AI Labs, an information-rich platform built to train AI for battlefield drones, marking the first time that Kyiv has opened up its trove of wartime data to an outside government, according to officials in London.

The announcement comes a month after U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham signed an AI deal with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy while visiting Kyiv alongside other allies to honor Ukraine’s independence day and pledge continued support to the war-torn nation.

“Ukraine is the frontline of freedom for us all. On my recent visit to Kyiv, I saw first-hand the courage and resilience of the Ukrainian people,” U.K. Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said in a statement on Friday.

“I also saw the extraordinary innovation which is allowing them to repel Putin’s illegal and unprovoked invasion.”

“This world-first access to real battlefield data will allow British companies to continue pushing the frontier of defence innovation, deterring our enemies and making us safer at home as well as further strengthening Ukraine,” Streeting said.

Ukraine has shared its combat-derived AI training data with allies in the past, but this is the first time that Kyiv has granted a foreign country access to the machine-learning infrastructure driving its rapid AI innovations seen across the front.

Avengers AI Labs holds an annotated dataset of more than 5 million battlefield frames, plus sensor data covering millions of object detections — including tanks, artillery, air defense, infantry, Shahed drones, reconnaissance UAVs, and more) — built mainly from Ukraine’s DELTA battle-management system, according to a release by Ukrainian officials.

Data is anonymized and released on a delay to avoid endangering personnel still fighting, according to Ukraine’s Defence Ministry. U.K. companies also work inside a secure perimeter that doesn’t allow them to download the underlying dataset, according to Ukraine’s MOD.

The British defense ministry is now inviting up to a dozen companies to submit proposals for how they would use the platform, especially to develop tech that would enable full functionality even when communications are degraded or satellite navigation is unavailable.

“It is exactly the kind of practical partnership the Taskforce was set up to drive, supporting our ally Ukraine while strengthening sovereign capability here in Britain,” U.K. AI Minister Kanishka Narayan said in Friday’s statement.

Katie Livingstone is the Ukraine correspondent for Defense News and Military Times. Based in Kyiv, she has covered Russia's full-scale invasion since its first days. She is a former Fulbright fellow whose award-winning work has appeared in outlets across Europe and the U.S.
items.titleZh: 乌克兰用于无人机技术的致命AI训练平台向英国公司开放
items.summaryZh: 乌克兰通过Avengers AI Labs向英国开放战时战场数据，使英国公司能够获取数据用于AI无人机研发。
items.zhFull:
基辅，乌克兰——据伦敦官员称，英国国防部已与乌克兰的 Avengers AI Labs 建立合作关系，该实验室是一个信息丰富的平台，旨在为战场无人机训练人工智能，这标志着基辅首次向外国政府开放其战时数据宝库。

这一消息宣布的一个月前，英国首相安迪·伯纳姆（Andy Burnham）在访问基辅期间与乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基（Volodymyr Zelenskyy）签署了一项人工智能协议，当时他与其他盟友一道前往基辅，纪念乌克兰独立日，并承诺继续支持这个饱受战争蹂躏的国家。

英国国防大臣韦斯·斯特里廷（Wes Streeting）在周五的一份声明中说：“乌克兰是我们所有人自由的前线。在我最近访问基辅期间，我亲眼目睹了乌克兰人民的勇气与坚韧。”

“我还看到了非凡的创新，正是这些创新让他们得以击退普京非法且无端的入侵。”

斯特里廷说：“这种全球首次获得的真实战场数据访问权限，将使英国公司能够继续推进国防创新的前沿，威慑我们的敌人，让我们在国内更安全，同时也进一步加强乌克兰。”

乌克兰过去曾与盟友分享其源自实战的人工智能训练数据，但这是基辅首次向外国开放其机器学习基础设施的访问权限，而正是这一基础设施推动着前线各地所见的人工智能快速创新。

据乌克兰官员发布的消息，Avengers AI Labs 拥有一个标注数据集，包含超过 500 万个战场帧，以及涵盖数百万次目标检测的传感器数据——包括坦克、火炮、防空系统、步兵、Shahed 无人机、侦察无人机等——主要构建自乌克兰的 DELTA 战场管理系统。

据乌克兰国防部称，数据经过匿名化处理并延迟发布，以避免危及仍在作战的人员。乌克兰国防部还表示，英国公司也在一个安全边界内工作，不允许下载底层数据集。

英国国防部目前正邀请至多12家公司提交方案，说明它们将如何使用该平台，尤其是开发相关技术，使平台即便在通信降级或卫星导航不可用时也能保持完整功能。

英国人工智能大臣卡尼什卡·纳拉扬（Kanishka Narayan）在周五的声明中表示：“这正该工作组旨在推动的那种务实伙伴关系，既支持我们的盟友乌克兰，又增强英国本土的主权能力。”

凯蒂·利文斯通（Katie Livingstone）是《防务新闻》和《军事时报》的乌克兰通讯员。她常驻基辅，自俄罗斯全面入侵最初几天起便持续进行报道。她曾是富布赖特学者，其获奖作品曾在欧洲和美国的多家媒体发表。

据乌克兰官员发布的消息，Avengers AI Labs 拥有一个标注数据集，包含超过 500 万个战场帧，以及涵盖数百万次目标检测的传感器数据——包括坦克、火炮、防空系统、步兵、Shahed 无人机、侦察无人机等——主要构建自乌克兰的 DELTA 战场管理系统。
据乌克兰国防部称，数据经过匿名化处理并延迟发布，以避免危及仍在作战的人员。乌克兰国防部还表示，英国公司也在一个安全边界内工作，不允许下载底层数据集。
英国国防部目前正邀请至多12家公司提交方案，说明它们将如何使用该平台，尤其是开发相关技术，使平台即便在通信降级或卫星导航不可用时也能保持完整功能。
英国人工智能大臣卡尼什卡·纳拉扬（Kanishka Narayan）在周五的声明中表示：“这正该工作组旨在推动的那种务实伙伴关系，既支持我们的盟友乌克兰，又增强英国本土的主权能力。”
凯蒂·利文斯通（Katie Livingstone）是《防务新闻》和《军事时报》的乌克兰通讯员。她常驻基辅，自俄罗斯全面入侵最初几天起便持续进行报道。她曾是富布赖特学者，其获奖作品曾在欧洲和美国的多家媒体发表。

items.title: Trump administration obligates $307M for military aid to Ukraine
items.author: Patricia Zengerle and Mike Stone, Reuters
items.summary: The Trump administration has made legally binding commitments to spend almost all of the $400 million Congress approved for military aid to Ukraine.
items.body:
The Trump administration has made legally binding commitments to spend almost all of the $400 million Congress approved for military aid to Ukraine late last year, ensuring that the money will not expire on Sept. 30, according to three sources familiar with the plan.

As of early this week, $307 million of the $400 million of the Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative (USAI) funding had been obligated, said the sources, who spoke on condition of anonymity, and the administration plans to lock in the remaining $93 million before the fiscal year ends on Sept. 30.

The Pentagon, which oversees the USAI program, declined to comment for this story.

First deliveries include weapons, spare parts

The money has been a source of contention with Congress, as Democrats and some of President Donald Trump’s fellow Republicans have criticized the Pentagon for sitting on the aid for Kyiv, which members of both parties voted for last December.

Trump has in recent months taken a more positive tone toward Ukraine, signing off on a proposal to give a license for Ukraine to manufacture Patriot interceptor missiles and signing a Russia sanctions bill.

He met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy this week at UN headquarters in New York, after which Zelenskiy said they had discussed efforts to end the war with Russia, including a potential bilateral ceasefire on energy-related targets.

The first deliveries, which will include offensive weapons and equipment such as spare parts for armored vehicles, began this month. The rest are expected to be delivered before October 2029, the sources said. Trump’s White House term ends in January of that year.

The remaining $93 million in the package approved by Congress does not have to be spent by the end of the year, but it will expire if it is not formally placed under contract by then.

Patriot missiles not included

One of the sources said the military equipment did not include Patriot missiles, despite Russia bombarding Ukraine’s cities with drones and ballistic missiles.

The U.S. war in Iran and the Ukraine war have depleted global supplies of Patriots, and Kyiv has been pleading for more.

Reuters reported in July that the administration had told Congress it could take years for the equipment to reach Ukrainian forces. The Pentagon has held up shipments of weapons to Ukraine several times out of concern that US weapons supplies were too low.

Lawmakers said then they were unhappy with the Pentagon’s timeline, considered unusually slow for an ongoing conflict, and the issue has come up repeatedly at congressional hearings.

Ukraine has been by far the top recipient of U.S. foreign aid since Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022, but the U.S. commitment to Kyiv has been called into question since Trump took office and his Republicans took control of both houses of Congress in January 2025.
items.titleZh: 特朗普政府拨定3.07亿美元对乌军事援助
items.summaryZh: 特朗普政府已作出具有法律约束力的承诺，将把国会批准的对乌克兰4亿美元军事援助中的几乎全部款项支出。
items.zhFull:
据三位了解该计划的消息人士称，特朗普政府已做出具有法律约束力的承诺，将把国会去年年底批准的4亿美元对乌军事援助资金几乎全部支出，确保这笔钱不会在9月30日到期作废。

消息人士称，截至本周初，乌克兰安全援助倡议（USAI）4亿美元资金中已有3.07亿美元完成拨付；这些要求匿名的消息人士表示，政府计划在9月30日本财年结束前锁定剩余的9300万美元。

负责监管USAI项目的五角大楼拒绝对此事置评。

首批交付包括武器和备件

这笔资金一直是与国会争执的焦点：民主党人和特朗普总统的一些共和党同僚批评五角大楼迟迟不发放对基辅的援助，而两党议员去年12月都投票支持了这笔援助。

近几个月，特朗普对乌克兰的语气更为积极，批准了一项允许乌克兰生产 Patriot 拦截导弹的提案，并签署了一项对俄制裁法案。

本周他在纽约联合国总部会见了乌克兰总统泽连斯基（Volodymyr Zelenskiy），会后泽连斯基表示，双方讨论了结束与俄罗斯战争的努力，包括可能就能源相关目标达成双边停火。

首批交付于本月开始，其中包括进攻性武器以及装甲车辆备件等装备。消息人士称，其余部分预计将在2029年10月前交付完毕。特朗普的白宫任期将于当年1月结束。

国会批准的这项一揽子计划中剩余的 9300 万美元无需在年底前支出，但如果届时未正式签订合同，这笔资金将失效。

未包含“爱国者”导弹

其中一名消息人士称，这批军事装备不包括“爱国者”导弹，尽管俄罗斯正用无人机和弹道导弹轰炸乌克兰的城市。

美国在伊朗的战争以及乌克兰战争已使全球“爱国者”导弹的库存消耗殆尽，基辅一直在恳求获得更多。

路透社 7 月报道称，该届政府已告知国会，这批装备可能需要数年时间才能送达乌克兰军队。由于担心美国武器库存过低，五角大楼已多次推迟向乌克兰运送武器。

议员们当时表示，他们对五角大楼的时间表感到不满，认为对于一场正在进行的冲突而言这一进度异常缓慢，该问题已在国会听证会上被反复提及。

自 2022 年 2 月俄罗斯发动全面入侵以来，乌克兰一直是美国对外援助的最大受援国，且远超其他国家和地区；但自特朗普（Trump）就职、其所属共和党于 2025 年 1 月控制国会两院以来，美国对基辅的承诺便受到质疑。

items.title: US appeals court upholds Pentagon’s blacklisting of Anthropic
items.author: Reuters
items.summary: A federal appeals court upheld the Pentagon’s blacklisting of Anthropic from military contracts, handing a victory to President Trump and the Pentagon.
items.body:
A federal appeals court on Friday upheld the Pentagon’s blacklisting of Anthropic from military contracts, handing a victory to President Donald Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in their battle with the AI startup over safety guardrails on its technology.

The 2-1 decision by the U.S. Court of Appeals in Washington came in a lawsuit by Anthropic challenging its March designation by the Pentagon as a national security supply chain risk, which the startup says has cost it billions of dollars in lost business and damaged its reputation ahead of a highly anticipated initial public offering.

The court’s majority said it was reasonable for the Pentagon to designate Anthropic after it refused to allow its products to be used for autonomous weapons or mass surveillance. It rejected Anthropic’s claim that the Pentagon had retaliated against it for its views on AI safety and ethics.

Siding with Hegseth’s argument that Anthropic’s safety restrictions could compromise military operations, the majority said, “The Secretary raises the deeply sobering prospect of overly constrained AI models shutting down unexpectedly and thus causing important military operations to fail,” in an opinion by Judge Gregory Katsas.

San Francisco-based Anthropic said in a statement Friday that it respectfully disagrees with the decision but remains confident in its position and is considering its options, including review of the three-judge panel’s decision by the full appeals court.

The White House and the Department of Defense did not immediately respond to emails seeking comment.

A federal judge in San Francisco last month struck down a parallel designation under a different law, finding the administration had unlawfully retaliated against Anthropic for its views on AI safety. U.S. District Judge Rita Lin in San Francisco also blocked Trump’s government-wide ban on Anthropic and Hegseth’s order barring military contractors from doing any business with the startup.

Hegseth designated Anthropic as a risk under two different laws after Anthropic refused to remove guardrails against its technology being used for autonomous weapons or mass domestic surveillance.

The unprecedented move came after months of negotiations ended in failure and public recriminations by Hegseth and Trump, who accused Anthropic of endangering American lives with ideological posturing.

Anthropic denied that characterization and said AI is not yet reliable enough to be safely used in autonomous weapons. The company also said it opposes domestic surveillance as a violation of fundamental rights.
items.titleZh: 美国上诉法院维持五角大楼将Anthropic列入黑名单的决定
items.summaryZh: 一家联邦上诉法院维持了五角大楼将Anthropic列入黑名单、禁止其获得军事合同的决定，这成为特朗普总统和五角大楼的一次胜利。
items.zhFull:
周五，一家联邦上诉法院维持了五角大楼将Anthropic列入军事合同黑名单的决定，这使总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)和国防部长皮特·海格塞斯(Pete Hegseth)在与这家AI初创公司就其技术安全护栏的争斗中获胜。

华盛顿的美国联邦上诉法院以2比1作出的这一裁决，源于Anthropic提起的诉讼，该公司质疑五角大楼在3月将其指定为国家安全供应链风险。这家初创公司称，这一指定使其损失了数十亿美元业务，并在备受期待的首次公开募股前损害了其声誉。

法院多数意见称，在Anthropic拒绝允许其产品被用于自主武器或大规模监控后，五角大楼将其指定为风险是合理的。法院驳回了Anthropic的说法，即五角大楼因其在AI安全与伦理方面的观点而对其实施报复。

多数意见支持海格塞斯的论点，即Anthropic的安全限制可能危及军事行动。在法官格雷戈里·卡察斯(Gregory Katsas)撰写的一份意见书中，多数意见称：“部长提出了一个令人深感警醒的前景：受到过度约束的AI模型意外关闭，从而导致重要军事行动失败。”

总部位于旧金山的Anthropic周五在一份声明中表示，它尊重但不同意该裁决，但对其立场仍抱有信心，并正在考虑各种选项，包括由全体上诉法院法官复审该三人法官合议庭的裁决。

白宫和国防部没有立即回应寻求置评的电子邮件。

上月，旧金山的一名联邦法官推翻了依据另一部法律作出的类似指定，认定政府因Anthropic在AI安全方面的观点而对其实施了非法报复。旧金山的美国地区法官丽塔·林(Rita Lin)还阻止了特朗普针对Anthropic的整个政府范围的禁令，以及海格塞斯禁止军事承包商与该初创公司开展任何业务的命令。

在Anthropic拒绝移除防止其技术被用于自主武器或大规模国内监控的护栏后，海格塞斯依据两部不同法律将其指定为风险。

这一史无前例的举动出台之前，长达数月的谈判以失败告终，赫格塞思（Hegseth）与特朗普还公开互相指责，他们指控Anthropic以意识形态作秀，危及美国人的生命。

Anthropic否认这一说法，并表示人工智能目前尚不够可靠，无法安全地用于自主武器。该公司还表示，反对国内监控，认为这侵犯了基本权利。

items.title: US Navy stands up hub to prepare unmanned systems for combat
items.author: Riley Ceder
items.summary: U.S. Chief of Naval Operations Adm. Daryl Caudle announced a new autonomous development center to train sailors and test new technology.
items.body:
The U.S. Navy announced Thursday a new development center that will train sailors to use autonomous technology in preparation for robotic systems to deploy across the entire fleet.

The service established the Robot and Autonomous Systems Warfighting Development Center at Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek, Virginia, ushering in a new era that will teach service members to be technically proficient while developing and fielding new combat-ready robotic systems.

“A prototype is not combat power,” Chief of Naval Operations Adm. Daryl Caudle said in a C-NOte message. “Combat power comes when a trained sailor can employ a reliable system, supported by the right networks, logistics, maintenance, software, tactics, authorities, and command relationships, to create an operational effect.”

The new center provides a place to work on autonomous system integration so that by the time sailors in the fleet get their hands on the technology, it is ready to be used.

RASWDC will first focus on training sailors at the center to understand the systems enough to employ them in combat, while developing a broader system for teaching that can be disseminated through the entire Navy to help service members learn the technology.

The center will help create warfighting concepts that delineate strict guidelines for how commanders build mission plans and set frameworks for autonomous systems to operate within. These guidelines become especially important when systems are forced to operate in combat environments where communication between robotic technology and the human in the loop is compromised.

RASWDC will also test emerging systems in environments that mimic those in which they will be deployed. Technology will be asked to perform at sea, under stress, against simulated threats and during degraded communication environments.

The systems that achieve their goal despite these obstacles will continue to be developed with the end goal of employing them on the battlefield, while others that fail will be retired.

Caudle defined the intended cycle as field, employ, learn, improve and scale.

Caudle released another C-NOte on Sept. 2, calling for the swift integration of lasers and their offensive capabilities into the fleet.

“The question is no longer whether these systems work — it is how quickly we can field them across the fleet and place them in the hands of sailors,” Caudle said.

On Tuesday, the Navy demonstrated a new information-sharing capability that allows it to streamline communication between operators and autonomous aircraft.

Riley Ceder is a Navy reporter at Military Times, where he covers issues directly affecting service members and their families, as well as breaking news.
items.titleZh: 美海军成立中心，为无人系统投入作战做准备
items.summaryZh: 美国海军作战部长 Adm. 达里尔·考德尔（Daryl Caudle）宣布成立一个新的自主系统发展中心，用于培训水兵并测试新技术。
items.zhFull:
美国海军周四宣布成立一个新的发展中心，将培训水兵使用自主技术，为机器人系统在全舰队范围内部署做好准备。

该军种在弗吉尼亚州利特尔克里克联合远征基地成立了机器人及自主系统作战发展中心，由此开启一个新时代：在培养军人技术精通能力的同时，研发并部署新型可投入作战的机器人系统。

“原型不等于战斗力，”海军作战部长 Adm. 达里尔·考德尔（Daryl Caudle）在一份 C-NOte 消息中表示。“战斗力来自一名受过训练的水兵能够运用可靠的系统，并得到合适的网络、后勤、维修、软件、战术、授权和指挥关系的支撑，从而产生作战效果。”

新中心提供了一个开展自主系统集成工作的场所，以便舰队水兵接触到相关技术时，该技术已经可以投入使用。

RASWDC 将首先专注于在该中心培训水兵，使其充分了解这些系统，从而能在战斗中使用它们，同时开发一套可在整个海军推广的、更广泛的教学体系，帮助军人学习相关技术。

该中心将协助制定作战概念，为指挥官如何制定任务计划划定严格准则，并为自主系统的运行设定框架。当系统被迫在机器人技术与在环人类之间通信受损的战斗环境中运行时，这些准则尤为重要。

RASWDC 还将在模拟其部署环境的场景中测试新兴系统。相关技术将被要求在海上、承受压力、面对模拟威胁以及通信降级的环境下运行。

在这些障碍下仍能达成目标的系统将继续研发，最终目标是将其用于战场；而未能通过考验的系统则将被淘汰。

考德尔（Caudle）将预期循环定义为：部署、运用、学习、改进和扩展。

9月2日，考德尔发布了另一份 C-NOte，呼吁将激光器及其进攻能力迅速集成到舰队中。

“问题不再是这些系统是否管用——而是我们多快能将它们部署到整个舰队，并交到水兵手中，”考德尔说。

周二，海军展示了一种新的信息共享能力，使其能够简化操作员与自主飞机之间的通信。

莱利·塞德（Riley Ceder）是《军事时报》（Military Times）的海军记者，负责报道直接影响军人及其家属的问题以及突发新闻。

items.title: Thales in ‘quite advanced’ talks with NATO countries on AI-powered command software
items.author: Rudy Ruitenberg
items.summary: French firm Thales is “quite advanced” in discussions with a number of NATO countries about using its artificial intelligence-powered C2 system.
items.body:
PARIS — French defense-technology firm Thales is “quite advanced” in discussions with a number of NATO countries about using its artificial intelligence-powered command-and-control system HexaForce, said the company’s vice president for multi-domain operations, Patrick Moreau.

Thales announced the availability of HexaForce last week, after testing it during NATO’s Coalition Warrior Interoperability Exercise, or CWIX, in Poland in June. The company is positioning the system as a multi-domain C2 “overlay” that can plug into legacy and national systems from the strategic to the tactical level, while allowing users to choose their own AI models and avoid vendor lock-in.

NATO is increasingly turning to AI to harness growing amounts of data in command and control, and already operates a C2 system supplied by United States-based Palantir Technologies. Meanwhile, the European Union is looking to accelerate development and deployment of European capabilities amid concern about sovereign control of the technology underpinning them.

“I don’t want to go too much into detail. but we are quite advanced in some discussions with some NATO countries so far,” Moreau told Defense News in a Sept. 24 interview.

As European and NATO militaries look to scale operations from brigade-level formations to army corps of more than 100,000 troops, AI will be key to processing more complex data, shortening planning cycles and improving situational awareness, Moreau said.

HexaForce is aimed at providing command and control from the army corps level down to the battalion, according to the executive. Thales defined a goal with end users to be able to plan 1,000 target missions a day, a tenfold increase.

The system has an open architecture built around NATO standards, allowing countries to plug in existing systems for tasks such as mission planning, or use the large language model of their choice, according to Moreau. In addition to the LLM component, HexaForce includes agentic AI for tasks such as targeting mission preparation.

It has a fully distributed architecture designed to rely on mesh capability, allowing the system to be spread over different data hubs within different command posts, in line with new operational concepts to not rely on central computing, according to Moreau.

By interfacing with legacy solutions, HexaForce can add “AI-powered capability” to systems already in use by the armed forces, according to Moreau. HexaForce is a command-and-control system, and users still need dedicated tactical systems to provide sensor data, he said.

The executive said the aim at CWIX was for end users to test HexaForce and its interoperability with existing and legacy systems. The system implements NATO standards related to the Data-Centric Security and Federation Mission Networking frameworks, he said.

For threats identified at the strategic command level, HexaForce can propose different courses of action, including firing options using air or land forces, according to Moreau. The operator can then choose a course of action, with the system sending the targeting mission to the tactical level.

“Of course it remains up to the operator to choose to push the button, and to choose the best option proposed by HexaForce,” Moreau said. “There is no automated action.”

In addition to connecting to systems that provide tactical awareness, Hexaforce could include commercial ship-tracking data or cyber threats to provide a more complete picture, Moreau said.

While developed with input from the French Army, the executive repeatedly stressed that the Thales system is designed as a NATO solution rather than a France-specific system. Asked how it compares with existing systems such as Systematic’s SitaWare or Airbus’s Multi-Domain Combat Cloud, Moreau instead focused on the interoperability of the Thales system.

Moreau said HexaForce is ready and already in the hands of the armed forces, with the first version taking nine months from design to making it available to the French Army.

France is developing its sovereign C2 system Arcadia, and Moreau said that while Hexaforce could be “a cornerstone” of the French system, the decision is not up to Thales.

Rudy Ruitenberg is a Europe correspondent for Defense News. He started his career at Bloomberg News and has experience reporting on technology, commodity markets and politics.
items.titleZh: 泰雷兹就人工智能赋能指挥软件与北约国家进行“相当深入”的谈判
items.summaryZh: 法国公司泰雷兹（Thales）正就使用其人工智能赋能的指挥控制（C2）系统与多个北约国家进行“相当深入”的讨论。
items.zhFull:
巴黎——法国国防科技公司泰雷兹（Thales）负责多域作战的副总裁帕特里克·莫罗（Patrick Moreau）表示，该公司正就使用其人工智能驱动的指挥控制系统HexaForce，与多个北约国家进行“相当深入”的讨论。

泰雷兹上周宣布HexaForce已可供使用。此前，该系统于6月在波兰举行的北约“联盟战士互操作性演习”（CWIX）期间进行了测试。该公司将该系统定位为一种多域C2“覆盖层”，可从战略到战术层面接入遗留系统和各国系统，同时允许用户选择自己的人工智能模型，避免供应商锁定。

北约正越来越多地借助人工智能来利用指挥控制中不断增长的数据量，并且已经在运行一套由总部位于美国的Palantir Technologies提供的C2系统。与此同时，欧盟正寻求加快欧洲能力的开发和部署，原因是担心对支撑这些能力的技术的主权控制问题。

“我不想说得太详细，但到目前为止，我们与一些北约国家的某些讨论已经相当深入，”莫罗在9月24日接受《防务新闻》（Defense News）采访时表示。

莫罗表示，随着欧洲和北约军队寻求将行动规模从旅级编队扩大到兵力超过10万人的军级单位，人工智能将成为处理更复杂数据、缩短规划周期和提高态势感知能力的关键。

这位高管表示，HexaForce旨在提供从军级到营级的指挥控制。泰雷兹与最终用户确定了一个目标，即能够每天规划1000个目标打击任务，相当于提高十倍。

莫罗表示，该系统采用围绕北约标准构建的开放架构，使各国能够接入现有系统以执行任务规划等任务，或使用其自行选择的大语言模型。除了大语言模型组件外，HexaForce还包含用于目标打击任务准备等任务的智能体式人工智能。

莫罗表示，该系统采用完全分布式架构，旨在依靠网状能力，使系统能够分布在不同指挥所内的不同数据中枢上，符合不依赖集中式计算的新作战概念。

据莫罗（Moreau）称，通过与遗留解决方案对接，HexaForce 可为武装部队已在使用的系统增添“AI 驱动能力”。他说，HexaForce 是一个指挥控制系统，用户仍需专用战术系统来提供传感器数据。

这位高管表示，在 CWIX 上的目标是让最终用户测试 HexaForce 及其与现有和遗留系统的互操作性。他说，该系统落实了北约与以数据为中心的安全和联邦任务网络框架相关的标准。

莫罗称，对于在战略指挥层识别出的威胁，HexaForce 可以提出不同的行动方案，包括使用空中或地面部队的火力选项。随后，操作员可以选择一种行动方案，系统会将目标打击任务发送至战术层。

“当然，是否按下按钮以及是否选择 HexaForce 提出的最佳方案，仍由操作员决定，”莫罗说，“没有自动化行动。”

莫罗说，除连接提供战术态势感知的系统外，HexaForce 还可纳入商业船舶跟踪数据或网络威胁，以提供更完整的态势图。

尽管该系统在开发过程中吸纳了法国陆军的意见，但这位高管反复强调，泰雷兹系统是按北约解决方案设计的，而非法国专用系统。当被问及与 Systematic 的 SitaWare 或空客的 Multi-Domain Combat Cloud 等现有系统相比如何时，莫罗反而着重谈到泰雷兹系统的互操作性。

莫罗说，HexaForce 已准备就绪，并已交付武装部队使用；首个版本从设计到提供给法国陆军耗时九个月。

法国正在开发其主权 C2 系统 Arcadia，莫罗表示，尽管 HexaForce 可能成为该法国系统的“基石”，但决定权不在泰雷兹。

鲁迪·鲁滕贝格（Rudy Ruitenberg）是《防务新闻》驻欧洲记者。他的职业生涯始于彭博新闻社，在技术、大宗商品市场和政治报道方面拥有丰富经验。

items.title: Desolate Arctic outpost likely to host US troops under new Greenland deal
items.author: Stine Jacobsen, Jacob Gronholt-Pedersen and Tom Little, Reuters
items.summary: Under a U.S. agreement signed this week, a small outpost at Mestersvig, Greenland, could soon become a key American military foothold in the Arctic.
items.body:
At a windswept gravel airstrip in eastern Greenland, a small Danish military detachment has quietly kept watch for decades.

Now, under a new U.S. defense agreement signed this week, the outpost at Mestersvig could soon become a key American military foothold in the Arctic.

Mestersvig sits 149 miles from the nearest settlement (population 330), at the edge of an uninhabited national park larger than Germany and France combined. The place is covered in darkness during winter, with average temperatures of around 14 degrees Fahrenheit.

“This is as remote, as cold, and as extreme as you can find in the world. You have to go to Antarctica to find similar conditions,” said Anders Ibsen, a former officer with Denmark’s Sirius dog sled patrol, an elite unit that uses Mestersvig to resupply.

It oversees the stretch of ocean between Greenland, Iceland and Britain — known as the GIUK gap — that Russia’s Northern Fleet must cross to reach the Atlantic. For NATO, controlling this chokepoint is critical to containing Russian naval power.

Local member of parliament Justus Hansen welcomed the expansion, saying, “In east Greenland, we really need that new money.”

Under the defense agreement, Washington will be allowed to establish a new base at Mestersvig and Narsarsuaq in southern Greenland, potentially marking the first U.S. military expansion on the vast, semi-autonomous Arctic island in decades.

Currently, only three soldiers maintain the facility, which was built in the 1960s and includes barracks to house 150 soldiers.

The U.S. has made no public announcement about its plans for the base.

A HISTORY OF OUTSIDE INTEREST

During World War II, this stretch of the Arctic island’s coast became a front line in the “weather war,” a race between Germany and the Allies to read Greenland’s weather, which shaped conditions over the North Atlantic and Europe days later.

Germany secretly built manned stations here, but Danish dog sled patrols tracked them down, and Allied forces drove them out.

Nearby, an EU-backed project aims to mine molybdenum — a critical metal for aerospace and defence — some 12 miles away. A Texas oil company plans to drill for oil this winter at an untested basin just south of Mestersvig, although it still lacks a permit to do so.

The previous owner, ARCO, spent heavily on seismic work in the 1970s but never drilled.

“Any infrastructural improvements in Greenland would be very welcome,” said Robert Price, CEO of Greenland Energy, the oil company.

The 1.1-mile airstrip — long enough for military transport planes to land — can collect up to 5 meters of snow a year.

“When it’s snowing, you’re basically removing snow 24/7,” said Ibsen, the former dog sled patrol officer who spent a year at Mestersvig.

“You have plenty to do just staying alive.”

items.summaryZh: 根据本周签署的一项美国协议，位于格陵兰 Mestersvig 的一座小型前哨站可能很快成为美国在北极的重要军事立足点。
items.zhFull:
在格陵兰东部一条寒风劲吹的砾石简易机场，一支丹麦小规模军事分遣队数十年来一直默默守望。

如今，根据本周签署的一项新美国防务协议，梅斯特斯维格前哨站可能很快成为美国在北极的重要军事立足点。

梅斯特斯维格距最近定居点（人口330）149 miles，位于一座面积超过德国和法国之和的无人国家公园边缘。冬季这里一片漆黑，平均气温约为14 degrees Fahrenheit。

“这里是世界上你能找到的最偏远、最寒冷、最极端的地方。要找到类似条件，你得去南极洲，”丹麦“天狼星”狗拉雪橇巡逻队前军官安德斯·易卜生（Anders Ibsen）说。这支部队是一支精锐单位，利用梅斯特斯维格进行补给。

该前哨站监控着格陵兰、冰岛和英国之间的海域——即GIUK缺口——俄罗斯北方舰队必须穿越该海域才能抵达大西洋。对北约而言，控制这一咽喉要道对于遏制俄罗斯海军力量至关重要。

当地议员尤斯图斯·汉森（Justus Hansen）对扩建表示欢迎，他说：“在格陵兰东部，我们确实需要这笔新资金。”

根据这项防务协议，华盛顿将被允许在梅斯特斯维格以及格陵兰南部的纳萨尔苏瓦克建立新基地，这可能标志着美国数十年来首次在这个广袤、半自治的北极岛屿上扩展军事存在。

目前，只有三名士兵维护该设施；该设施建于20世纪60年代，包括可容纳150名士兵的营房。

美国尚未公开宣布其对该基地的计划。

外部利益介入的历史

二战期间，这座北极岛屿的这段海岸线成为“气象战”的前线——德国与盟国竞相解读格陵兰的天气，而这里的天气会在数日后左右北大西洋和欧洲的气象状况。

德国曾在此秘密修建有人驻守的站点，但丹麦的狗拉雪橇巡逻队追踪到这些站点，盟军将其驱逐。

在附近，一个由欧盟支持的项目计划在大约12英里外开采钼——一种航空航天和国防领域的关键金属。一家得克萨斯石油公司计划今年冬天在 Mestersvig 正南方一个未经勘探的盆地钻探石油，尽管该公司尚未获得相应许可。

此前的所有者 ARCO 公司在20世纪70年代投入巨资进行地震勘探，但从未钻探。

“格陵兰的任何基础设施改善都会非常受欢迎，”石油公司 Greenland Energy 首席执行官罗伯特·普赖斯（Robert Price）说。

这条1.1英里长的简易跑道——足以供军用运输机降落——每年积雪可达5米。

“下雪的时候，你基本上一天到晚都在清雪，”曾在梅斯特斯维格待过一年的前狗拉雪橇巡逻队军官伊布森（Ibsen）说。

“光是活下去，你就有很多事要做。”

items.title: DAF to adopt standardized Religious Affiliation Codes: Action required in vMPF
items.author: Pentagon News
items.summary: Airmen and Guardians must take action to update their RAC in the Virtual Military Personnel Flight and certify their Record of Emergency Data is accurate.
items.body: A chaplain assigned to the 1st Special Operations Wing wears a religious insignia on his chest at Hurlburt Field, Florida, Aug. 19, 2026. Under Department of the Air Force guidance, effective June 15, 2026, chaplains transitioned to wearing religious insignia instead of officer rank on their Operational Camouflage Pattern uniforms to remove visual barriers and increase approachability for Air Commandos. (U.S. Air Force photo by Ashton Hamby)
items.titleZh: 空军部将采用标准化的宗教归属代码：须在 vMPF 中采取行动
items.summaryZh: 空军人员和太空军人员必须采取行动，在虚拟军事人事系统（vMPF）中更新其宗教归属代码（RAC），并确认其紧急数据记录准确无误。
items.zhFull: 一名隶属于第1特种作战联队的随军牧师于2026年8月19日在佛罗里达州赫尔伯特机场，胸前佩戴着宗教徽章。根据空军部自2026年6月15日起生效的指导意见，随军牧师已改为在作战迷彩服上佩戴宗教徽章，而非军官军衔，以消除视觉隔阂，并让空军特战人员更易于接近他们。（美国空军照片，由阿什顿·汉比（Ashton Hamby）拍摄）

items.title: AF Week in Photos
items.author: Pentagon News
items.summary: This week's photos feature Airmen from around the globe involved in activities supporting expeditionary operations and defending America. This weekly feature showcases the men and women of the Air Force.
items.body:
POW/MIA Remembrance Week Senior Airman Joseph Drewitz, an MQ-9 Reaper aircraft journeyman assigned to the 25th Aircraft Maintenance Squadron, participates in a ruck march at Nellis Air Force Base, Nev., Sept. 17, 2026. Participants completed events throughout POW/MIA Remembrance Week to honor the service and sacrifice of the nation’s prisoners of war and those who remain missing in action. (U.S. Air Force photo by Airman Isabella Borrillo)

POW/MIA Remembrance Week

Senior Airman Joseph Drewitz, an MQ-9 Reaper aircraft journeyman assigned to the 25th Aircraft Maintenance Squadron, participates in a ruck march at Nellis Air Force Base, Nev., Sept. 17, 2026. Participants completed events throughout POW/MIA Remembrance Week to honor the service and sacrifice of the nation’s prisoners of war and those who remain missing in action. (U.S. Air Force photo by Airman Isabella Borrillo)

Northern formation U.S. Air Force F-16 Fighting Falcons and a KC-135 Stratotanker fly in formation while conducting aerial refueling during Operation Arctic Vanguard over Greenland, Sept. 16, 2026. The joint and multinational operation enhances interoperability, tests cold-weather combat readiness and strengthens coalition capabilities across the Arctic region. (U.S. Air Force photo by Maj. David Brown)

U.S. Air Force F-16 Fighting Falcons and a KC-135 Stratotanker fly in formation while conducting aerial refueling during Operation Arctic Vanguard over Greenland, Sept. 16, 2026. The joint and multinational operation enhances interoperability, tests cold-weather combat readiness and strengthens coalition capabilities across the Arctic region. (U.S. Air Force photo by Maj. David Brown)

Cleared for takeoff Air Force running back Rocco Conti hurdles over a defender during a game against Duquesne University at the U.S. Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs, Colo., Sept. 5, 2026. Air Force shut out Duquesne 34-0 in its season opener. (U.S. Air Force photo by Jonathan Suni)

Cleared for takeoff

Air Force running back Rocco Conti hurdles over a defender during a game against Duquesne University at the U.S. Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs, Colo., Sept. 5, 2026. Air Force shut out Duquesne 34-0 in its season opener. (U.S. Air Force photo by Jonathan Suni)

Honor flight A U.S. Air Force F-35A Lightning II assigned to the 48th Fighter Wing flies a pattern before a ceremonial flyover at RAF Mildenhall, United Kingdom, Sept. 11, 2026. The formation flew over a 9/11 remembrance ceremony during the U.S. national anthem. (U.S. Air Force photo by Senior Airman Cody J. A. Mott)

A U.S. Air Force F-35A Lightning II assigned to the 48th Fighter Wing flies a pattern before a ceremonial flyover at RAF Mildenhall, United Kingdom, Sept. 11, 2026. The formation flew over a 9/11 remembrance ceremony during the U.S. national anthem. (U.S. Air Force photo by Senior Airman Cody J. A. Mott)

Leader of the pack Chief Master Sergeant of the Air Force David R. Wolfe conducts a question-and-answer session during the 2026 Air, Space and Cyber Conference at National Harbor, Md., Sept. 14, 2026. Wolfe emphasized team-driven combat readiness and the need to prepare adaptable Airmen to operate effectively amid uncertainty. (U.S. Air Force photo by Andy Morataya)

Leader of the pack

Chief Master Sergeant of the Air Force David R. Wolfe conducts a question-and-answer session during the 2026 Air, Space and Cyber Conference at National Harbor, Md., Sept. 14, 2026. Wolfe emphasized team-driven combat readiness and the need to prepare adaptable Airmen to operate effectively amid uncertainty. (U.S. Air Force photo by Andy Morataya)

Buddy lift Airmen conduct hoist operations from a CV-22 Osprey during a demonstration at Kirtland Air Force Base, N.M., Sept. 14, 2026. The flight was part of a two-day celebration commemorating 20 years of CV-22 aircrew training at Kirtland AFB. (U.S. Air Force photo by Airman Maurice Casilla)

Airmen conduct hoist operations from a CV-22 Osprey during a demonstration at Kirtland Air Force Base, N.M., Sept. 14, 2026. The flight was part of a two-day celebration commemorating 20 years of CV-22 aircrew training at Kirtland AFB. (U.S. Air Force photo by Airman Maurice Casilla)

Preparing for takeoff Capt. Logan Baldwin, a 20th Bomb Squadron pilot, prepares for takeoff aboard a B-52H Stratofortress at Barksdale Air Force Base, La., Aug. 30, 2026. Bomber Task Force missions enable crews to maintain a high state of readiness and proficiency while validating the Air Force’s always-ready global strike capability. (U.S. Air Force photo by Senior Airman Rhea Beil)

Preparing for takeoff

Capt. Logan Baldwin, a 20th Bomb Squadron pilot, prepares for takeoff aboard a B-52H Stratofortress at Barksdale Air Force Base, La., Aug. 30, 2026. Bomber Task Force missions enable crews to maintain a high state of readiness and proficiency while validating the Air Force’s always-ready global strike capability. (U.S. Air Force photo by Senior Airman Rhea Beil)

Two of a kind Two F-15E Strike Eagles assigned to the 4th Fighter Wing emerge through clouds over North Carolina, Sept. 12, 2026. The aircraft flew in tandem with a KC-46A Pegasus assigned to the 916th Air Refueling Wing during aerial refueling operations that also supported a flyover at NC Freedom Fest in Goldsboro, N.C. (U.S. Air Force photo by Senior Airman Hudson Steiner)

Two of a kind

Two F-15E Strike Eagles assigned to the 4th Fighter Wing emerge through clouds over North Carolina, Sept. 12, 2026. The aircraft flew in tandem with a KC-46A Pegasus assigned to the 916th Air Refueling Wing during aerial refueling operations that also supported a flyover at NC Freedom Fest in Goldsboro, N.C. (U.S. Air Force photo by Senior Airman Hudson Steiner)

Lighting the way A U.S. Air Force Special Operations Command loadmaster holds an LUU-2C/B illuminating flare aboard an MC-130J Commando II during airdrop training off the coast of Okinawa, Japan, Sept. 9, 2026. During the training, loadmasters released the flares to provide target training for F-22 Raptor weapons systems. (U.S. Air Force photo by Senior Airman Melany Bermudez)

Lighting the way

A U.S. Air Force Special Operations Command loadmaster holds an LUU-2C/B illuminating flare aboard an MC-130J Commando II during airdrop training off the coast of Okinawa, Japan, Sept. 9, 2026. During the training, loadmasters released the flares to provide target training for F-22 Raptor weapons systems. (U.S. Air Force photo by Senior Airman Melany Bermudez)

Fueling the fight A B-52H Stratofortress assigned to the 5th Bomb Wing, Minot Air Force Base, N.D., receives fuel from a KC-135 Stratotanker assigned to the 185th Air Refueling Wing, Iowa Air National Guard, over South Dakota, Sept. 15, 2026. The 185th ARW aircrew conducted the impromptu refueling after completing a separate aerial refueling mission with a B-1B Lancer in the area. (U.S. Air Force photo by Staff Sgt. John Johnson)

Fueling the fight

A B-52H Stratofortress assigned to the 5th Bomb Wing, Minot Air Force Base, N.D., receives fuel from a KC-135 Stratotanker assigned to the 185th Air Refueling Wing, Iowa Air National Guard, over South Dakota, Sept. 15, 2026. The 185th ARW aircrew conducted the impromptu refueling after completing a separate aerial refueling mission with a B-1B Lancer in the area. (U.S. Air Force photo by Staff Sgt. John Johnson)

Simulation evacuation Maj. Paul Pikman, a Critical Care Air Transport Team physician, and Maj. Owen Caron, a CCATT registered nurse, perform a simulated patient medical evacuation during exercise Ultimate Caduceus 2026 at Scott Air Force Base, Ill., Sept. 8, 2026. After receiving the simulated patient, the medical professionals conducted a medical assessment before transferring the patient to another aircraft for transport. (U.S. Air Force photo by Airman 1st Class Izcalli X. Martinez)

Maj. Paul Pikman, a Critical Care Air Transport Team physician, and Maj. Owen Caron, a CCATT registered nurse, perform a simulated patient medical evacuation during exercise Ultimate Caduceus 2026 at Scott Air Force Base, Ill., Sept. 8, 2026. After receiving the simulated patient, the medical professionals conducted a medical assessment before transferring the patient to another aircraft for transport. (U.S. Air Force photo by Airman 1st Class Izcalli X. Martinez)

No runway required A U.S. Air Force C-130J Super Hercules assigned to the 37th Airlift Squadron operates from a sand landing zone in Rømø, Denmark, during exercise Northern Viking 26, Aug. 25, 2026. Operating from varied surfaces reduces reliance on established airfields and gives commanders additional options to disperse, position and sustain forces. (U.S. Air Force photo by Senior Airman Edgar Grimaldo)

No runway required

A U.S. Air Force C-130J Super Hercules assigned to the 37th Airlift Squadron operates from a sand landing zone in Rømø, Denmark, during exercise Northern Viking 26, Aug. 25, 2026. Operating from varied surfaces reduces reliance on established airfields and gives commanders additional options to disperse, position and sustain forces. (U.S. Air Force photo by Senior Airman Edgar Grimaldo)

items.summaryZh: 本周图片展示了全球各地空军人员参与支持远征行动和保卫美国的活动。这一每周专题展示空军的男女官兵。

战俘/失踪人员纪念周 第25飞机维修中队 MQ-9 Reaper 飞机专业兵、高级空军士兵约瑟夫·德鲁维茨（Joseph Drewitz）于2026年9月17日在内华达州内利斯空军基地参加负重行军。参与者在战俘/失踪人员纪念周期间完成各项活动，以纪念美国战俘的服役与牺牲以及仍在行动中失踪的人员。（美国空军照片，由空军士兵伊莎贝拉·博里略拍摄）

荣誉飞行 一架隶属于第48战斗机联队的美国空军 F-35A Lightning II 于2026年9月11日在英国米尔登霍尔皇家空军基地进行仪式性飞越前飞航线。该编队在奏美国国歌期间飞越了一场9/11纪念仪式。（美国空军上等兵科迪·J·A·莫特（Cody J. A. Mott）摄）

items.title: France to send military to protect Saudi Arabia on Red Sea oil route, Macron says
items.author: Reuters
items.summary: France will send troops and defense systems to Saudi Arabia to help protect the Red Sea port city of Yanbu, which is key for energy transport, Macron said.
items.body:
PARIS, Sept 24 (Reuters) — France will send troops and defense systems to Saudi Arabia to help protect the Red Sea port city of Yanbu, which is key for energy transport, French President Emmanuel Macron said on Thursday.

Macron also said a U.S. ban on diesel exports, which the White House has denied is under consideration, would be “catastrophic,” both globally and for the U.S. economy.

Macron was speaking in a wide-ranging primetime television interview on the international situation, in which he also warned about possible Russian attacks on French soil.

Facing growing pressure at home over high energy prices, Macron sought to assure the French that France had adequate gas and oil supplies as winter approaches. He said Paris was actively working to ensure flows were not disrupted.

Crude oil prices have surged recently as the main alternative route for Saudi oil exports through Yanbu has come under missile attacks from Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis.

“We are going to send military resources, that is to say, soldiers, radar systems and defense systems, to protect this site — not to get us involved in any conflicts, but to protect this site,” Macron told TF1 and France 2 TV.

Macron dismissed a report by Spanish newspaper El Mundo that the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency had warned European governments about the threat of potential drone attacks from the Mediterranean.

“I can deny it. The CIA did not inform French services,” he said.

Still, Macron said Russia is multiplying hostile and criminal acts against European countries, and France could face strikes similar to the failed attack in Leipzig. Germany said Russia was responsible for an attempted drone attack in August on the Leipzig airport.

Macron gathered French party chiefs at the Elysee last week to brief them on the growing threat from Russia. He later said he had ordered his government to draw up a plan to protect critical infrastructure against drone and cyber attacks.

Macron said Moscow was seeking to intimidate Europe and break the continent’s resolve in supporting Ukraine.

Russia says European allegations of hybrid attacks are baseless and the result of anti-Russian hysteria.

Yet Macron’s position on Russia was weakened this week after France shocked other EU members by getting Russian-Uzbek metals tycoon Alisher Usmanov exempted from EU sanctions, citing national security concerns. That prompted Azerbaijan to pardon a French national jailed for espionage.
items.titleZh: 马克龙称法国将派兵保护沙特红海石油航线
items.summaryZh: 马克龙表示，法国将向沙特阿拉伯派遣部队和防御系统，以帮助保护红海港口城市延布，该地对能源运输至关重要。
items.zhFull:
巴黎，9月24日（路透社）——法国总统马克龙（Emmanuel Macron）周四表示，法国将向沙特阿拉伯派遣部队和防御系统，以帮助保护红海港口城市延布，该地对能源运输至关重要。

马克龙还表示，美国禁止柴油出口——白宫否认正在考虑这一举措——无论对全球还是对美国经济而言都将是“灾难性的”。

马克龙是在一次内容广泛的黄金时段电视采访中就国际形势发表上述言论的，他在采访中还警告称俄罗斯可能对法国本土发动袭击。

面对国内因能源价格高企而日益增大的压力，马克龙试图让法国人放心，随着冬季临近，法国拥有充足的天然气和石油供应。他说，巴黎正在积极努力确保供应不中断。

近期原油价格大幅飙升，原因是沙特石油出口经由延布的主要替代路线遭到也门受伊朗支持的胡塞武装的导弹袭击。

“我们将派遣军事资源，也就是说，士兵、雷达系统和防御系统，来保护这一地点——不是让我们卷入任何冲突，而是为了保护这一地点，”马克龙对TF1和France 2电视台表示。

马克龙否认了西班牙《世界报》（El Mundo）的一篇报道，该报道称美国中央情报局曾就来自地中海的潜在无人机袭击威胁向欧洲各国政府发出警告。

“我可以否认这一点。中情局没有通知法国情报部门，”他说。

尽管如此，马克龙 (Macron) 表示，俄罗斯正在不断增加针对欧洲国家的敌对和犯罪行为，法国可能面临与莱比锡未遂袭击类似的打击。德国表示，俄罗斯应对8月针对莱比锡机场的一起未遂无人机袭击负责。

马克龙上周在爱丽舍宫召集法国各党派领袖，向他们通报来自俄罗斯的日益增长的威胁。他随后表示，已命令政府制定一项计划，保护关键基础设施免受无人机和网络攻击。

马克龙表示，莫斯科正试图恐吓欧洲，并瓦解欧洲大陆支持乌克兰的决心。

俄罗斯表示，欧洲关于混合攻击的指控毫无根据，是反俄歇斯底里的结果。

然而，本周马克龙在俄罗斯问题上的立场遭到削弱，此前法国以国家安全关切为由，使俄罗斯-乌兹别克金属大亨阿利舍尔·乌斯马诺夫 (Alisher Usmanov) 获得欧盟制裁豁免，令其他欧盟成员国感到震惊。这促使阿塞拜疆赦免了一名因间谍罪入狱的法国公民。

items.title: Sixth powerful attack submarine departs Barrow-in-Furness for sea trials
items.summary: UK and Euro-Atlantic security will soon be boosted, as the Royal Navy’s sixth powerful attack submarine departs from Barrow-in-Furness.
items.body:
Latest Astute Class submarine, HMS Agamemnon has sailed from the BAE Systems shipyard in Barrow-in-Furness.

She will now undergo sea trials – a major step towards delivering the highly capable attack submarine to bolster security for the UK and the Euro-Atlantic.

The UK’s submarine industrial base is benefitting from £6 billion of Government investment over the Spending Review period and sustains thousands of jobs.

The newest Royal Navy conventionally armed nuclear-powered submarine, HMS Agamemnon and nicknamed ‘Awesome Aggie’, will now begin sea trials - a period of testing ahead of joining active service with the Royal Navy.

The Astute Class are the largest, most advanced and most powerful attack submarines ever operated by the Royal Navy. Weighing 7,400 tonnes and at 97 metres long, they are just short of the length of two Olympic swimming pools. Powered by a Rolls-Royce Submarines nuclear reactor, produced in Derby in the Midlands, the submarine will not need to refuel for the duration of her service life.

The submarine’s high-tech capabilities include stealthy precision strike, anti-submarine warfare, and intelligence gathering. HMS Agamemnon will be armed with heavyweight Spearfish torpedoes and Tomahawk IV land attack missiles, able to strike targets at a range of more than 1,000 miles.

Alongside their role supporting the continuous at sea deterrent, Astute-class submarines are also involved in protecting maritime task groups and providing support to UK, NATO and coalition operations.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said:

Having seen first-hand the dedication and pride of the workforce in Barrow, and that of the thousands of people who work across our submarine supply chain in the United Kingdom, I know how much this milestone will mean to each and every one of them. As one of the most advanced submarines ever built, HMS Agamemnon will play a major role in further boosting our security here at home and across NATO.

Having seen first-hand the dedication and pride of the workforce in Barrow, and that of the thousands of people who work across our submarine supply chain in the United Kingdom, I know how much this milestone will mean to each and every one of them.

As one of the most advanced submarines ever built, HMS Agamemnon will play a major role in further boosting our security here at home and across NATO.

Defence Secretary, Wes Streeting MP said:

Deterrence is the bedrock of our national security. Another formidable attack submarine going to sea strengthens that deterrence and demonstrates how we are stepping up to meet the threats of a more dangerous world. I’ve been on board HMS Agamemnon and met her submariners and the skilled workers who delivered this incredible feat of engineering. It’s a powerful reminder of how strengthening our defence creates good jobs, opens up opportunity, and reindustrialises our country.

Deterrence is the bedrock of our national security. Another formidable attack submarine going to sea strengthens that deterrence and demonstrates how we are stepping up to meet the threats of a more dangerous world.

I’ve been on board HMS Agamemnon and met her submariners and the skilled workers who delivered this incredible feat of engineering. It’s a powerful reminder of how strengthening our defence creates good jobs, opens up opportunity, and reindustrialises our country.

HMS Agamemnon’s departure from Barrow-in-Furness is the result of years of work by a highly skilled workforce. This includes the engineers, technicians and specialists at BAE Systems and the Defence Nuclear Enterprise (DNE), together with the ship’s company who will take her into service. Their combined expertise reflects the depth of skill sustained in Barrow and across the UK’s submarine enterprise.

Maddy McTernan, Chief of Defence Nuclear, said:

HMS Agamemnon’s departure is a significant moment for the UK’s Defence Nuclear Enterprise and is a clear demonstration of the engineering and industrial excellence of the Barrow workforce and across the wider UK supply chain. Submarine production will continue to boost British industry for decades to come backed by the commitments announced in the recent Defence Investment Plan.

Submarine production will continue to boost British industry for decades to come backed by the commitments announced in the recent Defence Investment Plan.

Royal Navy First Sea Lord, General Sir Gwyn Jenkins, said:

In an increasingly dangerous world, sea power remains fundamental to keeping our country and people safe. Our submarine fleet is essential to that effort, which is why I am delighted that HMS Agamemnon, the sixth of our Astute-class submarines, has now begun sea trials and will soon arrive at HMNB Clyde to join the fleet. She embodies the best of British engineering and the professionalism of our submariners and will be one of the most advanced submarines ever operated by the Royal Navy. As we continue to strengthen our warfighting readiness, HMS Agamemnon will play a central role in keeping the United Kingdom safe, contributing to NATO’s collective defence and ensuring we are ready to lead, fight and win.

In an increasingly dangerous world, sea power remains fundamental to keeping our country and people safe. Our submarine fleet is essential to that effort, which is why I am delighted that HMS Agamemnon, the sixth of our Astute-class submarines, has now begun sea trials and will soon arrive at HMNB Clyde to join the fleet.

She embodies the best of British engineering and the professionalism of our submariners and will be one of the most advanced submarines ever operated by the Royal Navy.

As we continue to strengthen our warfighting readiness, HMS Agamemnon will play a central role in keeping the United Kingdom safe, contributing to NATO’s collective defence and ensuring we are ready to lead, fight and win.

Building on commitments to continuous submarine production made in the 2025 Strategic Defence Review, and reinforced in the Defence Investment Plan (DIP), the completion of HMS Agamemnon demonstrates the strength and reliability of British industry and its world-leading nuclear technology.

The DIP is backed by £298 billion over the next four years, including £47 billion for investment in our submarine build programmes, which also covers maintenance and infrastructure. Part of that spend will enable the UK to produce a submarine every 18 months in support of the SSN-AUKUS programme.

Recognising Barrow’s role as a strategic national asset, DNE spending is fuelling substantial growth and expansion in the town. The economic certainty from the government’s commitment to the submarine building programme underpins the 10-year Plan for Barrow, backed by the £200 million Barrow Transformation Fund. More than 14,000 roles in Barrow-in-Furness are supported by defence nuclear work, with 1,800 additional roles created in Barrow under this government.

HMS Agamemnon has been delivered as part of a national endeavour by the MOD’s DNE, the partnership organisations that operate, maintain, renew and sustain the UK’s nuclear deterrent. The DNE supports over 47,000 jobs across the UK, including thousands of highly-skilled roles involved in submarine production.

Marking entry into the Royal Navy, HMS Agamemnon was formally commissioned by His Majesty the King in a ceremony on 22 September 2025. She is the sixth Navy vessel to bear the name.

The seventh and final submarine in the class, Achilles, is at an advanced stage of construction in Barrow. The Astute Class will be succeeded by up to 12 new SSN-AUKUS nuclear-powered attack submarines from the late 2030s, with steel due to be cut for the first-in-class in Barrow next year, continuing the town’s role at the heart of AUKUS delivery.
items.titleZh: 第六艘强大的攻击型潜艇离开巴罗因弗内斯进行海试
items.summaryZh: 随着皇家海军第六艘强大的攻击型潜艇从巴罗因弗内斯出发，英国及欧洲-大西洋安全将很快得到加强。
items.zhFull:
最新一艘机敏级潜艇 HMS Agamemnon 已从位于巴罗因弗内斯的 BAE Systems 造船厂驶出。

她现将接受海试——这是向交付这艘能力强大的攻击潜艇、以加强英国和欧洲-大西洋地区安全迈出的重要一步。

在支出审查期间，英国潜艇工业基础正受益于政府 £6 billion 投资，并维持数千个就业岗位。

英国皇家海军最新一艘常规武器核动力潜艇 HMS Agamemnon，绰号“Awesome Aggie”，现将开始海试——这是加入皇家海军现役前的一段测试期。

机敏级是英国皇家海军有史以来操作过的最大、最先进和最强力的攻击潜艇。它们重达 7,400 tonnes，长 97 metres，仅比两个奥林匹克游泳池的长度短一点。该潜艇由在英格兰中部德比生产的罗尔斯·罗伊斯潜艇核反应堆提供动力，在服役期内将无需更换核燃料。

该潜艇的高科技能力包括隐蔽精确打击、反潜战和情报收集。HMS Agamemnon 将配备重型 Spearfish 鱼雷和 Tomahawk IV 对陆攻击导弹，能够打击超过 1,000 miles 范围内的目标。

除了支持持续海上威慑任务外，机敏级潜艇还参与保护海上任务群，并为英国、北约和联军行动提供支持。

首相安迪·伯纳姆（Andy Burnham）表示：

亲眼目睹巴罗（Barrow）员工以及英国潜艇供应链数千名员工的奉献与自豪，我深知这一里程碑对他们每一个人将有多么重要。作为有史以来建造的最先进潜艇之一，HMS Agamemnon将在进一步加强我们本土及整个北约的安全方面发挥重要作用。

亲眼目睹巴罗（Barrow）员工以及英国潜艇供应链数千名员工的奉献与自豪，我深知这一里程碑对他们每一个人将有多么重要。

作为有史以来建造的最先进潜艇之一，HMS Agamemnon将在进一步加强我们本土及整个北约的安全方面发挥重要作用。

国防大臣、议员韦斯·斯特里廷（Wes Streeting）表示：

威慑是我们国家安全的基石。又一艘强大的攻击型潜艇出海，增强了这一威慑，并表明我们正在加大力度应对一个更加危险的世界所带来的威胁。我曾登上HMS Agamemnon，会见了该艇潜艇兵以及完成这一惊人工程壮举的技术工人。这有力提醒我们，加强国防如何创造优质就业、开拓机遇，并推动我国再工业化。

HMS Agamemnon驶离巴罗因弗内斯（Barrow-in-Furness），是一支技能高超的员工队伍多年努力的成果。这包括BAE Systems和国防核企业（Defence Nuclear Enterprise，DNE）的工程师、技术人员和专家，以及将接舰服役的全舰官兵。他们的综合专长反映了巴罗及英国潜艇产业所保持的技能深度。

在我们持续强化作战战备之际，HMS Agamemnon 将在保障英国安全方面发挥核心作用，为北约集体防御作出贡献，并确保我们随时准备领导、作战并取胜。

2025年战略防务评估中作出的持续建造潜艇的承诺，在《防务投资计划》（DIP）中得到进一步强化；HMS Agamemnon 的完工表明，英国工业及其世界领先的核技术具备强大实力与可靠性。

《防务投资计划》在未来四年获得2980亿英镑支持，其中470亿英镑用于投资潜艇建造项目，也涵盖维护与基础设施。部分支出将使英国能够每18个月建造一艘潜艇，以支持 SSN-AUKUS 计划。

巴罗作为国家战略资产的地位得到认可，国防核企业（DNE）的支出正推动该镇大幅增长与扩张。政府对潜艇建造计划的承诺所带来的经济确定性，为巴罗十年计划提供支撑，该计划由2亿英镑的巴罗转型基金支持。巴罗因弗内斯有超过14000个岗位依靠国防核工作维持，本届政府执政期间在巴罗新增1800个岗位。

items.title: US F-35 fighters to debut in Indian multinational air exercise
items.author: Anjana Pasricha
items.summary: The participation of F-35 stealth fighters in the Indian drills signals that New Delhi’s and Washington’s defense ties remain steady.
items.body:
NEW DELHI — The U.S. Air Force’s F-35 fighter jets are joining a multinational air exercise hosted by India, bringing a fifth-generation fighter to Indian air drills for the first time and giving the Indian Air Force and other participants direct exposure to operating alongside an advanced stealth aircraft.

The drills get underway Saturday at the Jodhpur air base in Rajasthan state, which lies about 200 kilometers from India’s border with Pakistan. Eight countries are participating and 32 more are attending as observers.

India does not have a fifth-generation fighter aircraft. It will deploy its major fighters such as Rafales, Su-30MKIs, Tejas and the Mirage 2000 in the combat drills. France is bringing Rafale jets and the United Arab Emirates is bringing F-16s.

At a time when India’s rival China is rapidly expanding its fleet of fifth-generation fighters, the exercise could give the Indian Air Force a first-hand experience of tactical missions with advanced stealth aircraft and gain insight into how such jets can integrate sensor data, operate as part of a networked force and complicate detection by adversary radars.

Indian vice chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, said as the character of warfare changes, the drills, named “Tarang Shakti,” will help participants prepare for the challenges “of tomorrow.”

“We do not conduct Tarang Shakti to demonstrate what we already know. We conduct it to discover what we still need to learn,” he told reporters on Wednesday. “Our partners bring their own operational experience. Bringing these together in a realistic training environment allows us to test assumptions, challenge procedures, understand different methods of employing air power and improve interoperability.”

The participation of F-35 stealth fighters in the Indian drills also underscores that New Delhi’s and Washington’s defense ties remain on a steady keel, despite their broader relationship coming under some strain over trade disputes and India’s purchases of Russian oil.

While the U.S. stealth fighter has twice featured at defense exhibitions in India and the Indian Air Force operated alongside F-35s during joint exercises in Australia two years ago, the upcoming drill marks the first time the aircraft will undertake tactical missions with Indian fighters from an Indian airbase.

Dixit said the air force also wants to use the air exercises to test lessons learned during India’s brief conflict with Pakistan in May last year in which both countries deployed fighter jets.

Besides the United States, France and UAE, other countries bringing air assets like surveillance and transport aircraft are Germany, Australia, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Greece.

The drills are being held soon after India held bilateral air exercises with Japan in which Tokyo deployed its fighter aircraft, the Mitsubishi F-2A fighter aircraft in India for the first time. That exercise, held Sept. 9-22, was seen as a signal of growing defense ties between New Delhi and Tokyo amid an assertive China in the Indo-Pacific.

“Our partnership has progressed beyond simply conducting exercises together to refining our tactical capabilities at a practical level,” Japan’s Air Self-Defense Force Chief of Staff Gen. Takehiro Morita said Sept. 20 in Jodhpur where the drill was conducted.

The multinational air drill starting Saturday will conclude on Oct. 12.
items.titleZh: 美国F-35战斗机将首次亮相印度多国空军演习
items.summaryZh: F-35隐身战斗机参加印度演习，表明新德里与华盛顿之间的防务关系保持稳定。
items.zhFull:
新德里——美国空军的F-35战斗机正在参加印度主办的多国空中演习，这是第五代战斗机首次参加印度空中演习，使印度空军和其他参与者能够直接体验与先进隐形飞机协同作战。

演习将于周六在拉贾斯坦邦的焦特布尔空军基地开始，该基地距离印度与巴基斯坦边境约200公里。八个国家参演，另有32个国家作为观察员出席。

印度没有第五代战斗机。它将在此次作战演习中部署其主力战斗机，如Rafale、Su-30MKI、Tejas和Mirage 2000。法国将派出Rafale战斗机，阿拉伯联合酋长国将派出F-16。

在印度的对手中国迅速扩充其第五代战斗机机队之际，此次演习可能使印度空军获得使用先进隐形飞机执行战术任务的第一手经验，并深入了解此类战机如何整合传感器数据、作为网络化部队的一部分作战，以及如何使敌方雷达更难探测。

印度空军副参谋长阿舒托什·迪克西特（Ashutosh Dixit）空军中将表示，随着战争性质的变化，代号“塔朗·沙克蒂”的演习将帮助参与者为“明天”的挑战做好准备。

“我们举行‘塔朗·沙克蒂’演习不是为了展示我们已经知道的东西。我们举行演习是为了发现我们仍需学习的内容，”他周三告诉记者。“我们的伙伴带来了他们自己的作战经验。将这些经验汇聚在逼真的训练环境中，使我们能够检验假设、挑战程序、了解运用空中力量的不同方法并提高互操作性。”

F-35隐形战斗机参加印度演习也凸显出，尽管新德里与华盛顿的整体关系因贸易争端和印度购买俄罗斯石油而承受一定压力，但两国的防务关系仍保持稳定。

尽管美国隐形战斗机曾两次在印度的防务展上亮相，且印度空军两年前在澳大利亚的联合演习中曾与F-35协同行动，但即将举行的演习标志着该型飞机首次从印度空军基地与印度战斗机一起执行战术任务。

迪克西特（Dixit）表示，印度空军还希望借助此次空中演习，检验去年5月印度与巴基斯坦短暂冲突中汲取的经验教训，当时两国均出动了战斗机。

除美国、法国和阿联酋外，其他派出监视与运输机等空中装备的国家还包括德国、澳大利亚、孟加拉国、斯里兰卡和希腊。

此次演习举行前不久，印度刚与日本举行双边空中演习，东京首次将其战斗机——三菱F-2A战斗机部署至印度。该演习于9月9日至22日举行，被视为在印太地区中国日益强势的背景下，新德里与东京防务关系不断加深的信号。

“我们的伙伴关系已超越仅仅共同举行演习的阶段，进入了在实际层面精进战术能力的阶段，”日本航空自卫队航空幕僚长森田武宏（Takehiro Morita）上将9月20日在演习举办地焦特布尔说。

这场于周六开始的多国空中演习将于10月12日结束。
